conviction_note: Net of four items: a deferred divestiture gain that should flatter headline GAAP EPS versus the lone -$0.05 estimate (+1.5), against a FY27 revenue-growth target that H1 arithmetic has already made unreachable (-2.0), a post-dated competitor read that the shared fire-services demand driver was soft in exactly Lakeland's fiscal Q2 (-1.2), and a leverage-covenant ratio that mechanically deteriorates when a $5.1m EBITDA quarter rolls out of LTM (-1.0); sized small because the stock is already 34.6% off its 52w high and fell into the print.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 10-Q says the gain on the HPFR/HiViz sale attributable to inventory Lakeland still manufactures and ships for the buyer 'has been deferred and will be recognized over the six-month contract period' (27 Mar - 27 Sep 2026) — so a further tranche of divestiture gain lands inside fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026) on top of the $6,467k already booked in Q1, and the single published estimate is -$0.05.
findings.why_not_priced: The mechanic exists only in one sentence of a business-combination/disposal note; no wire story, no press release and no transcript quantifies the deferred portion. If it were priced the single estimate would not sit at -$0.0475 GAAP, and the Q1 coverage would have flagged that the $0.04 of Q1 'net income' was entirely a $6.5m asset-sale gain (ex-gain operating loss ~$4.2m vs -$4.6m prior year) rather than reporting a turnaround. On a 48,885-share ADV name the first print reaction is driven by the headline EPS line.
findings.independence: The size and existence of the gain is corroborated independently by the Q4/Q1 call commentary ($14m proceeds, $6.5m gain): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/09/lakeland-lake-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ . Note this finding and the covenant finding both touch the same 10-Q document — they are separate paragraphs (disposal note vs credit-agreement note) but share the filing.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY27 'high single-digit revenue growth' target is arithmetically out of reach: FY26 was $192.6m, Q1 FY27 was $47.4m (+1.4%) and the Q2 estimate is $51.48m (-2% vs the $52.5m year-ago quarter), so H1 is ~$99m and H2 must deliver ~$107m against H2 FY26's $93.4m, i.e. ~+15%, with the divested HPFR/HiViz lines absent from the whole second half.
findings.why_not_priced: No aggregator carries a quarterly revenue series for this name — the number has to be built from four separate releases (Q1 FY26 $46.7m, Q2 FY26 $52.5m, Q4 FY26 $45.8m, FY26 $192.6m implying Q3 $47.6m). The one covering analyst has a Buy and raised the target to $18 on 11 June 2026 against an $11.33 spot; if the H2 ramp were understood as a stretch that target would not be 59% above the price. A guidance trim on this call reads to the tape as a cut, not as arithmetic anyone had already done.
findings.independence: Management themselves pre-framed Q2 as 'a stepping stone rather than the full measure of the improvement opportunity' with the improvement in H2, which is the same H2-loaded shape: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/09/lakeland-lake-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-09). Points the same direction as the MSA finding below on revenue, but via a different mechanism and a different source.

findings.finding: MSA Safety, the largest fire-service PPE competitor, said on 30 July 2026 that fire-service orders tied to Assistance to Firefighters Grants 'came in more slowly than expected' in the quarter with fire-service revenue slightly down year on year — a read on Lakeland's single largest product line (49% of revenue) covering almost exactly Lakeland's fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026), and issued seven weeks after Lakeland last spoke.
findings.why_not_priced: MSA is a $9bn NYSE industrial and Lakeland a ~$115m Nasdaq microcap with one covering analyst; the read-across is never written up. If it had been priced, LAKE's 20-day run-up would not be only -6.75% and the Q2 revenue estimate would have moved off $51.48m, which implies roughly +7-10% organic growth once the divested HPFR/HiViz lines are stripped from the $52.5m comp — the opposite of what MSA described. The offsetting half (MSA said June/July momentum improved and FEMA wants to accelerate 2026 grant deliveries) is why this is sized under the implied-move scale rather than at it.
findings.independence: The underlying grant-cycle slippage is independently visible in FEMA's own calendar: the FY2025 AFG application window did not open until 19 May 2026, pushing grant-funded turnout-gear awards out by roughly a year — https://www.fema.gov/press-release/20260518/dhs-makes-648-million-available-help-firefighters-and-first-responders (2026-05-18).

findings.finding: Lakeland was out of compliance with its revolver covenants at 31 Jan 2026 and needed a limited waiver; the 10-Q sets the funded-debt/EBITDA cap at 3.5x stepping down to 3.25x on 1 Feb 2026 and 3.0x on 1 Feb 2027, and at 30 Apr 2026 the $23.8m drawn against ~$7.7m LTM adjusted EBITDA ex-FX (Q2 FY26 $5.1m + Q3 $0.2m + Q4 $1.3m + Q1 FY27 $1.1m) is ~3.1x — but the $5.1m quarter rolls out of LTM at 31 July, and no 8-K has been filed since 18 June 2026 despite management saying in June they were pursuing an asset-based lending replacement.
findings.why_not_priced: The waiver disclosure sits in the FY26 results release and the covenant step-down schedule in the 10-Q; connecting them to the quarterly adjusted-EBITDA series is arithmetic nobody publishes for a name with one analyst. If the market had priced a second covenant event the stock would not be +49% off its 52-week low, and the absence of any 8-K since 18 June — with a material new credit facility being an Item 1.01 event — would have been noticed. This is the lowest-confidence item here: management said in April they 'anticipate to be in covenant throughout fiscal 2027', covenant EBITDA has add-backs I cannot see, and $13.2m of divestiture proceeds plus $5.8m of Q1 operating cash could have paid the revolver down.
findings.independence: The waiver itself is confirmed from a different document, the FY26 results release: 'As of January 31, 2026, the Company was not in compliance with certain covenants under its revolving credit agreement. After January 31, 2026, the Company received a limited waiver' — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/04/16/3275796/0/en/lakeland-fire-safety-reports-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2026-financial-results.html (2026-04-16). Shares the 10-Q with finding 1.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider Form 4s: the three 2026-08-04 and four 2026-07-13 filings are code-F tax withholding at ~$11.40, not an open-market cluster in either direction
13G/A filings: BlackRock at 1.6% and Royce at 13.37%, both with a 30 June 2026 event date, i.e. routine quarterly amendments, not an off-cycle exit
No 8-K of any kind since 2026-06-18 — no pre-announcement, no credit amendment, no executive change, no acquisition; the 2026-06-18 8-K is only the 2026 equity plan and clean annual-meeting votes
The 2026-09-01 investor-conference release contains no business or financial update
No CEO/CFO transition: Jenkins has held President/CEO plus Executive Chairman since 2024/2023, so the 'CEO/Executive Chairman' styling in the September release is not new

Could not source a dollar figure for HPFR/HiViz product-line revenue — the FY26 10-K, the Q1 FY27 10-Q, both earnings releases and both transcripts disclose $14m of proceeds and a $6.5m gain but never the revenue being removed

PFAS: only a $0.064m adjustment in Q1 FY27 and no new litigation disclosure; NFPA 1970 recertification deadline of 18 March 2026 has passed and management frames the standard change as demand-positive, not as a liability

The sell-side and wire layer (single estimate -$0.0475 / $51.482m, DA Davidson $18 target of 2026-06-11) — read only to establish what is priced; the September 2025 Zacks and WallStreetZen rating changes surfacing in search are 2025 items, not current
baseline_tension: There is no option chain and therefore no skew to agree or disagree with, so the only priced statement is the -6.75% 20-day run-up into the print, which my net -2.7 agrees with — that agreement is the main reason I have sized well inside a name that routinely moves high single digits on prints; separately the sweep's year-ago comp of $0.36 is wrong, Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS was $0.08 on $52.5m of sales, so the 'earnings collapse' framing built on that row is meaningless and should not be treated as an independent bear point.
